column1: # Hadith 4 — Creation in the womb and the decree (Ibn Rajab's commentary, batch 1)

column2: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ — and he is the truthful, the one confirmed as truthful — told us: “The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop (nuṭfah);

then he becomes a clinging clot (ʿalaqah) for a like period; then he becomes a lump of flesh (muḍghah) for a like period. Then Allah sends the angel to him, who breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded with four things: to write down his provision, his deeds and his lifespan,

and whether he is wretched or happy. By the One besides whom there is no god, one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a forearm’s length between him and it; then what has been written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it.

And one of you does the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a forearm’s length between him and it; then what has been written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

The authenticity of this hadith is agreed upon, and the nation has received it with acceptance. Al-Aʿmash narrated it from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ibn Masʿūd, and it is by way of him that the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] recorded it in their two Ṣaḥīḥs.

It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Asfāṭī said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ in a dream and said: O Messenger of Allah, the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd which he narrated from you, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us, and he is the truthful, the one confirmed as truthful —

He ﷺ said: “By the One besides whom there is no god, I narrated it to him,” saying it three times. Then he said: May Allah forgive al-Aʿmash as he narrated it, and may Allah forgive those who narrated it before al-Aʿmash and those who narrated it after him.
It has also been narrated from Ibn Masʿūd by other routes.
His words ﷺ, “The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop,” have an explanation reported from Ibn Masʿūd.

Al-Aʿmash reported from Khaythamah that Ibn Masʿūd said: When the drop settles in the womb, it flies into every hair and nail and stays forty days; then it descends into the womb and becomes a clinging clot.
He said: That is its gathering.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others recorded it.

An explanation of the gathering with another meaning is also reported as marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ). Al-Ṭabarānī, and Ibn Mandah in Kitāb al-Tawḥīd, recorded from the hadith of Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When Allah the Exalted wills to create a servant and the man has intercourse with the woman,

his fluid flies into every vein and limb of hers. When it is the seventh day, Allah gathers it, then brings to it every vein [of ancestry] it has back to Ādam: ‘in whatever form He willed, He assembled you’ [al-Infiṭār 82:8].” Ibn Mandah said: Its chain is connected and well known, meeting the standard of Abū ʿĪsā [al-Tirmidhī], al-Nasāʾī and others.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and al-Ṭabarānī recorded, in the narration of Muṭahhar ibn al-Haytham, from Mūsā ibn ʿUlayy ibn Rabāḥ, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ said to his grandfather: “So-and-so, what has been born to you?”
He said: O Messenger of Allah, what could be born to me?
Either a boy or a girl. He said: “And whom does it resemble?”
He said: Whom could it resemble?

It resembles its mother or its father. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not say that. When the drop settles in the womb, Allah brings to it every lineage between it and Ādam. Have you not read this verse: ‘in whatever form He willed, He assembled you’ [al-Infiṭār 82:8]?

He said: He threaded you [through them].” This chain is weak; Muṭahhar ibn al-Haytham is very weak. Al-Bukhārī said: It is a hadith that is not authentic. He mentioned, with his chain, from Mūsā ibn ʿUlayy,
from his father, that his father did not become Muslim until the time of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — meaning that he was not a Companion.
This meaning is supported by the Prophet’s words ﷺ to the man who said to him, My wife has given birth to a black boy: “Perhaps a strain [of ancestry] drew it out.”
His words, “then he becomes a clinging clot for a like period,” mean forty days. A clinging clot is a piece of blood.
“Then he becomes a lump of flesh for a like period” — that is, forty days.
A lump of flesh is a piece of flesh.
“Then Allah sends the angel to him, who breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded with four things: to write down his provision, his deeds, his lifespan, and whether he is wretched or happy.”
This hadith shows that he passes through three stages over a hundred and twenty days, each forty days a stage: in the first forty he is a drop,
in the second forty a clinging clot, and in the third forty a lump of flesh; then, after the hundred and twenty days, the angel breathes the soul into him and writes these four things for him.
Allah has mentioned in many places in the Qurʾān how the foetus passes through these stages, as in His words, Exalted is He:

“O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, [know that] We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, so that We may make clear to you; and We settle in the wombs whatever We will for an appointed term” [al-Ḥajj 22:5].
He mentioned these three stages — the drop, the clinging clot and the lump of flesh — in a number of places in the Qurʾān, and in another place He mentioned more besides, saying in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn:

“We created man from an extract of clay; then We made him a drop in a firm lodging; then We made the drop a clinging clot, and We made the clot a lump of flesh, and We made the lump bones, and We clothed the bones with flesh; then We brought him forth as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators” [al-Muʾminūn 23:12–14].
These are seven stages that Allah mentions in this verse for the creation of the son of Ādam before the soul is breathed into him.

Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The son of Ādam was created from seven, and then recite this verse. He was asked about coitus interruptus, and he recited this verse and then said: Is anyone created until this description has run its course in him?
In one report from him he said: Does any soul die before it has passed through this creation?

It is reported that Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ said: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, al-Zubayr and Saʿd sat with me among a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they discussed coitus interruptus and said: There is no harm in it. A man said: They claim it is the lesser burying alive. ʿAlī said:

It is not burying alive until it has passed through the seven stages: it is an extract of clay, then a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then flesh, then another creation. ʿUmar said: You have spoken truly; may Allah prolong your life.
Al-Dāraquṭnī reported it in al-Muʾtalif wa-l-Mukhtalif.
A group of jurists permitted a woman to abort what is in her womb as long as the soul has not been breathed into it, treating it like coitus interruptus. This is a weak view,

because the foetus is a child that has been formed and may already have taken shape, whereas with coitus interruptus there is no child at all; it is only a means of preventing one from forming — and coitus interruptus may not prevent its forming if Allah wills to create it,
as the Prophet ﷺ said when asked about coitus interruptus: “You lose nothing if you do not do it, for there is no soul destined to exist but Allah is its Creator.”
The scholars of our school have stated explicitly that once the child has become a clinging clot, it is not permissible for the woman to abort it,
because it is a child that has been formed, unlike the drop, which has not yet formed and may never form into a child.

Some narrations of the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd mention the bones, and that he is bones for forty days. Imam Aḥmad recorded, in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Zayd: I heard Abū ʿUbaydah narrate, saying: ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“The drop stays in the womb for forty days in its state, unchanged. When the forty have passed, it becomes a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh likewise, then bones likewise. When Allah wills to fashion its creation, He sends an angel to it,” and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.
It is reported, from the hadith of ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When the drop settles in the womb,
it stays forty nights; then it is a clinging clot for forty nights, then a lump of flesh for forty nights, then bones for forty nights; then Allah clothes the bones with flesh.”
Imam Aḥmad’s narration indicates that the foetus is clothed with flesh only after a hundred and sixty days, and this is undoubtedly a mistake,
for after a hundred and twenty days the soul is undoubtedly breathed into him, as will be mentioned. ʿAlī ibn Zayd is Ibn Judʿān, and he is not relied upon as proof.
The hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd contains something indicating that flesh and bones are created at the start of the second forty. In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd,

the Prophet ﷺ said: “When forty-two nights have passed over the drop, Allah sends an angel to it, who shapes it and creates its hearing, its sight, its skin, its flesh and its bones. Then he says: My Lord, male or female?
And your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes it down. Then he says: My Lord, his term?
And your Lord says what He wills, and the angel writes it down. Then he says: My Lord, his provision?
And your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes it down. Then the angel goes out with the scroll in his hand, and adds nothing to what he was commanded and takes nothing from it.”

The apparent meaning of this hadith is that the shaping of the foetus and the creation of its hearing, sight, skin, flesh and bones take place at the start of the second forty, from which it follows that in the second forty it is flesh and bones.

Some have interpreted this to mean that the angel divides the drop, when it has become a clinging clot, into parts, making some for the skin, some for the flesh and some for the bones, and so measures all of it out before it exists.

This goes against the apparent meaning of the hadith; rather, its apparent meaning is that he shapes it and creates all these parts. The creation of these may consist in its being shaped and divided before the flesh and bones exist; and this may happen in some foetuses and not in others.

The hadith of Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith cited above indicates that the drop too is shaped, on the seventh day. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “Indeed, We created man from a drop, a mingling (amshāj)” [al-Insān 76:2], and a group of the Salaf explained the amshāj of the drop as the veins in it.
Ibn Masʿūd said: Its amshāj are its veins.
The medical scholars have mentioned what agrees with this. They said: When semen falls into the womb, it becomes frothy and foamy for six or seven days,
and in these days the drop is shaped without drawing on the womb; after that it draws on it. Lines and points begin three days after this, sometimes a day earlier or a day later.
Then, after six days — which is the fifteenth day from conception — blood penetrates all of it and it becomes a clinging clot. Then the organs become plainly distinct,

separating from contact with one another, and the moisture of the spinal marrow extends. Then, after nine days, the head separates from the shoulders, and the limbs from the digits, with a distinctness that is clear in some and hidden in others.
They said: The shortest time in which a male takes shape is thirty days; the usual time for the foetus to take shape is thirty-five days; and it may take shape in forty-five days.

They said: No complete male has been found among miscarriages before thirty days, nor a female before forty days. This agrees with what the hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd indicates about its being formed in the second forty and becoming flesh in it too.
Some have taken the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd to mean that in the first forty the foetus is predominantly characterised as semen, in the second forty as a clinging clot,
and in the third forty as a lump of flesh, even if its form has already been completed and its shaping finished. The hadith of Ibn Masʿūd does not mention when the foetus is shaped.
Something is reported from Ibn Masʿūd himself indicating that its shaping may also take place before the third forty. Al-Shaʿbī reported from ʿAlqamah,
from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: When the drop settles in the womb, an angel comes to it, takes it in his palm and says: My Lord, formed or unformed? If it is said:
Unformed, it does not become a living being, and the womb casts it out. If it is said: Formed, he says: My Lord, male or female?
Wretched or happy? What is the term? What of its footsteps?
In what land will it die?
He said: Then the drop is asked: Who is your Lord?
It says: Allah. It is asked: Who provides for you?

It says: Allah. It is said: Go to the Book, for you will find in it the story of this drop. He said: Then it is created, lives out its term, eats its provision and treads in its footsteps, until, when its term comes, it dies and is buried in that [place].

Then al-Shaʿbī recited this verse: “O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, [know that] We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed” [al-Ḥajj 22:5].

When it reaches the stage of a lump of flesh, it is turned into the fourth creation and becomes a living being. If it is unformed, the womb casts it out as blood; and if it is formed, it is turned into a living being.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others recorded it.
It is reported by another route from Ibn Masʿūd that there is no shaping before eighty days. Al-Suddī reported from Abū Mālik, and from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās,

and from Murrah al-Hamdānī, from Ibn Masʿūd, and from some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: “It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills” [Āl ʿImrān 3:6],

that he said: When the drop falls into the wombs, it flies through the body for forty days; then it is a clinging clot for forty days; then a lump of flesh for forty days. When it is time for it to be formed,

Allah sends an angel to shape it. The angel brings some dust between two of his fingers, mixes it into the lump of flesh and kneads it with it, then shapes it as he is commanded, and says: Male or female?
Wretched or happy? What is his provision?
What is his lifespan, and what his footsteps? What are his afflictions?
Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, speaks, and the angel writes. When that body dies, it is buried where that dust was taken from. Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī recorded it in his Tafsīr;

but opinion on al-Suddī is divided, and Imam Aḥmad used to object to his combining several chains for a single interpretation, just as he and others objected to al-Wāqidī’s combining several chains for a single hadith.

Groups of jurists adopted the apparent meaning of this narration and interpreted the marfūʿ hadith of Ibn Masʿūd in its light. They said: The shortest time in which the child’s form becomes discernible is eighty-one days,
because it only becomes a lump of flesh in the third forty, and it does not take form before it is a lump of flesh.

On this basis the scholars of our school and al-Shāfiʿī’s followers said: The waiting period (ʿiddah) does not end, nor is an umm walad freed, except by [the miscarriage of] a formed lump of flesh, and the earliest it can take form and shape is eighty-one days.

Aḥmad said of the clinging clot: It is blood in which no form is discernible. If the lump of flesh is unformed, does the waiting period end with it, and does the slave-woman become an umm walad by it?

There are two views, which are two reported positions of Aḥmad. If no outline appears in it, but it is hidden and recognisable only by women with expertise, and they testify to that, their testimony is accepted.

According to most scholars it makes no difference whether this is after four full months or before. Imam Aḥmad stated this explicitly in the narration of many of his followers, and his son Ṣāliḥ transmitted from him, concerning the infant, that its form becomes discernible within the four [months].

Al-Shaʿbī said: When it has been turned into the fourth creation, it is formed; the waiting period ends with it, and the slave-woman is freed by it, if it is at four months. Ḥanbal likewise transmitted from him [Aḥmad]: If an umm walad miscarries,

then if it was fully formed, she is freed, and the waiting period ends with it, when it has entered the fourth creation at four months, when the soul is breathed into it. This differs from what the many narrators reported from him.

In one reported position, Aḥmad said: When its form has become discernible, there is no disagreement that she is freed by it, if she is a slave-woman. A number of narrators also transmitted from him, concerning the clinging clot, that when it is clear that it is a child, the slave-woman is freed by it.

This is the view of al-Nakhaʿī, and it has been related as a view of al-Shāfiʿī. Some of the scholars of our school extended this reported position of Aḥmad to the ending of the waiting period by it as well.
All of this rests on its being possible for form to appear in the clinging clot, as may be argued from the hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd cited above — unless it is said

that the hadith of Ḥudhayfah only shows that it takes form once it has become flesh and bone, and that this may happen in the second forty, not while it is a clinging clot. This is open to question; Allah knows best.

What the physicians have mentioned shows that the clinging clot takes form and outline, and midwives likewise testify to it; and the hadith of Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith attests to shaping while the foetus is still a drop. Allah the Exalted knows best.

It remains, in the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, that after it has become a lump of flesh the angel is sent to it, writes the four things and breathes the soul into it, and that all of this is after a hundred and twenty days.

The wordings of the narrations of this hadith differ on the order of the writing and the breathing. In al-Bukhārī’s narration in his Ṣaḥīḥ: “And the angel is sent to him and is commanded with four things,
then he breathes the soul into him.” This narration states explicitly that breathing the soul comes after the writing. In a narration that al-Bayhaqī recorded in Kitāb al-Qadar:
“Then the angel is sent and breathes the soul into him; then he is commanded with four things.” This narration states explicitly that the breathing comes before the writing.
Either this comes from the narrators’ handling of their narrations, reporting according to the meaning they understood, or what is meant is only the order of telling, not the order of what is told.

In any case, the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd indicates that the breathing of the soul into the foetus, and the angel’s writing of his affair, are delayed until after four months, when the third forty is complete.
As for the breathing of the soul, it is reported explicitly from the Companions that the soul is breathed into it only after four months, as the apparent sense of the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd indicates.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī reported from his father, from ʿAlī, who said: When the drop has completed four months, an angel is sent to it and breathes the soul into it in the darknesses; that is His words, Exalted is He: “then We brought him forth as another creation” [al-Muʾminūn 23:14]. Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded it, and its chain is broken.

Al-Lālakāʾī recorded, with his chain of narration, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: When the drop falls into the womb, it stays four months and ten [days]; then the soul is breathed into it; then it stays forty nights;

then an angel is sent to it, who strikes it on the hollow of the nape and writes [it down as] wretched or happy. Its chain is open to question, and it states that the breathing of the soul comes ten days after the four months.

Imam Aḥmad based his well-known position on the apparent sense of the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd: that the soul is breathed into the child after the four months, and that if it is miscarried after four full months, the funeral prayer is prayed over it,
since the soul had been breathed into it and it had then died.

This is also related from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and it is one of the views of al-Shāfiʿī and of Isḥāq. More than one person transmitted that Aḥmad said: When it reaches four months and ten [days], the soul is breathed into it during those ten days, and the funeral prayer is prayed over it.

He said, in the narration of Abū al-Ḥārith from him: The living being is a drop for forty nights, a clinging clot for forty nights and a lump of flesh for forty nights; then it becomes bone and flesh; and when four months and ten [days] are complete, the soul is breathed into it.

The apparent sense of this narration is that the soul is breathed into it only after four months and ten [days] are complete, as was reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; while the narrations from Aḥmad before this one only indicate that the soul is breathed into it during the ten days after the four [months] are complete.
This is what is well known from him. Ibn al-Musayyib likewise said, when asked about the waiting period after a husband’s death being set at four months and ten [days]: Why the ten?
He said: The soul is breathed in during them.

As for the physicians, they mention that if the foetus takes shape in thirty-five days, it moves at seventy days and is born at two hundred and ten days, which is seven months; it may come some days earlier
or later in shaping and birth. If the shaping is at forty-five days, it moves at ninety days and is born at two hundred and seventy days, which is nine months. Allah knows best.
As for the angel’s writing, the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd indicates that it too comes after the four months, as has been seen. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Anas,
the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah has appointed an angel over the womb, who says: My Lord, a drop! My Lord, a clinging clot! My Lord, a lump of flesh! And when Allah wills to complete a creation, he says:”
“My Lord, male or female?
Wretched or happy? What is the provision? What is the term?
And so it is written while it is in its mother’s womb.” The apparent sense of this agrees with the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd,
but it does not specify a period. The hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd cited above indicates that the writing takes place at the beginning of the second forty.

Muslim also recorded it with another wording, from the hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd, who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The angel enters upon the drop after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights, and says: My Lord, wretched or happy?
And both are written down. Then he says: My Lord, male or female?
And both are written down; and his deeds, his footsteps, his term and his provision are written. Then the scrolls are rolled up, and nothing is added to them or taken from them.”
In another version in Muslim: “The drop falls into the womb for forty nights; then the angel comes upon it and says: My Lord, male or female?” and he mentioned the hadith.
In yet another version in Muslim: “for forty-odd nights.”
In the Musnad of Imam Aḥmad, from the hadith of Jābir, the Prophet ﷺ said: “When the drop has settled in the womb for forty days, or forty nights, an angel is sent to it and says:”
“My Lord, wretched or happy? And it is made known.”
We have already given what al-Shaʿbī reported from ʿAlqamah, from Ibn Masʿūd, as his own words, and its apparent sense indicates that the angel is sent to it while it is still a drop.

It is also reported from Ibn Masʿūd by two other routes that he said: “The deeds of the children of Ādam are presented to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, every day, and He looks into them for three hours;

then the wombs are brought, and He looks into them for three hours — that is His words, ‘He shapes you in the wombs however He wills’ [Āl ʿImrān 3:6], and His words, ‘He grants females to whom He wills’ [al-Shūrā 42:49]; then the provisions are brought,

and He looks into them for three hours; and the angels glorify Him for three hours. He said: This is your affair and the affair of your Lord.” But this does not fix any period for the looking into the wombs.

It is reported from a number of the Companions that the writing takes place in the second forty. Al-Lālakāʾī recorded, with his chain of narration, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: When the drop has stayed in the woman’s womb for forty nights, an angel comes to it,

snatches it up and ascends with it to the All-Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic, and says: Create, O best of creators. Allah decrees concerning it whatever He wills of His command, and then at that point it is handed to the angel, who says: My Lord, miscarried or complete?
And it is made clear to him. Then he says: My Lord, a short term or a full term?
And it is made clear to him. He says: My Lord, single or twin?
And it is made clear to him. He says: My Lord, male or female?
And it is made clear to him. Then he says: My Lord, wretched or happy?
And it is made clear to him. Then he says: My Lord, apportion his provision for him; and He apportions his provision for him along with his term, and he descends with both together.
By the One in whose hand is my soul, he will attain nothing of this world except what has been allotted to him.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, with his chain of narration, that Abū Dharr said: Semen stays in the womb for forty nights; then the angel of souls comes to it and ascends with it to the Compeller, the Mighty and Majestic, and says: My Lord, male or female?
And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, decrees what He decrees. Then he says: My Lord, wretched or happy?
And all that lies ahead of him is written down. Then Abū Dharr recited from the opening of Sūrat al-Taghābun up to His words:
“and He shaped you and made your shapes excellent, and to Him is the return” [al-Taghābun 64:3].
All of this agrees with what is in the hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd.
We have already seen, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the angel’s writing comes forty nights after the soul is breathed in, and that its chain is open to question.
Some have reconciled these hadiths and reports with the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd by affirming two writings; and it may be said besides that one of them is in heaven and the other in the mother’s womb.

The more likely view — and Allah knows best — is that it happens once, and perhaps this varies from one foetus to another: for some it is written after the first forty, and for others after the third forty.
It may also be said that the word “then” in the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd is meant only to order the telling, not to order what is told as it is in itself. Allah knows best.

One of the later scholars preferred the view that the writing takes place at the beginning of the second forty, as the hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd indicates, and said: Its mention in the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd was put after the mention of the lump of flesh,
even though it is introduced with the word “then”, so as not to break up the mention of the three stages through which the foetus passes, namely being a drop, a clinging clot and a lump of flesh;

for mentioning these three in one sequence is more striking and more elegant. That is why what is joined to them was put after them, even though it comes before some of them in order. He cited as evidence for this His words, Exalted is He:
“And He began the creation of man from clay; then He made his offspring from an extract of a despised fluid; then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit” [al-Sajdah 32:7–9].
Man here means Ādam (peace be upon him), and it is known that his fashioning and the breathing of the soul into him came before his offspring were made from an extract of a despised fluid.
But since the aim was to mention the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in beginning the creation of Ādam and the creation of his offspring, He joined the one to the other,

and put the mention of Ādam’s fashioning and the breathing of the soul into him afterwards, even though that came between Ādam’s creation from clay and the creation of his offspring. Allah knows best.
It has come that this writing is written between the eyes of the foetus. In the Musnad of al-Bazzār, from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both),
the Prophet ﷺ said: “When Allah creates the living soul, the angel of the wombs says: My Lord, male or female?
He said: And Allah decrees His command to him. Then he says: My Lord, wretched or happy?
And Allah decrees His command to him. Then he writes between its eyes what it will meet, even the misfortune that will befall it.”

It has also been reported as mawqūf on Ibn ʿUmar (his own words), not marfūʿ. The hadith of Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd cited above is explicit that the angel writes this in a scroll; perhaps he writes it in a scroll and also writes it between the child’s eyes.
It is reported that this writing is accompanied by the creation, along with the foetus, of the qualities it records, which become part of him. It is reported from ʿĀʾishah
that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When Allah wills to create a creature, He sends an angel, who enters the womb and says: My Lord, what?
He says: A boy, or a girl, or whatever Allah wills to create in the womb. He says: My Lord, wretched or happy?
He says: Whatever Allah wills. He says: My Lord, what is his term?
He says: Such-and-such. He says: What is his make? What are his traits?”
“He says: Such-and-such. There is nothing but it is created with him in the womb.”
Abū Dāwūd recorded it in Kitāb al-Qadar, and al-Bazzār in his Musnad.

In any case, this writing which is written for the foetus in its mother’s womb is other than the writing of the decrees that preceded the creation of creatures, mentioned in His words, Exalted is He: “No affliction befalls in the earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before We bring it into being” [al-Ḥadīd 57:22],
as in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah decreed the measures of creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.”
And in the hadith of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The first thing Allah created was the Pen, and He said to it: Write; and it flowed with what will be until the Day of Resurrection.”

We have already mentioned what is reported from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him): that when the angel asks about the state of the drop, he is commanded to go to the prior Book, and is told: You will find in it the story of this drop. The texts mentioning the prior Writ
of felicity and wretchedness are many. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“There is no soul destined to exist but Allah has written its place in Paradise or the Fire, and has written it as wretched or happy.” A man said:
O Messenger of Allah, shall we not then rely on what is written for us and leave off action?

He said: “Act, for each is eased towards what he was created for. As for the people of felicity, they are eased towards the deeds of the people of felicity; and as for the people of wretchedness, they are eased towards the deeds of the people of wretchedness.” Then he recited: “As for one who gives and is mindful of Allah” [al-Layl 92:5].

This hadith shows that felicity and wretchedness have been written beforehand, that this is decreed in accordance with deeds, and that each is eased towards the deeds he was created for, which are the means to felicity or wretchedness.
In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: A man said:
O Messenger of Allah, are the people of Paradise known from the people of the Fire?
He said: “Yes.” He said: Then why do those who act, act?
He said: “Each acts for what he was created for — or for what he is eased towards.”
This meaning has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ by many routes; and the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd shows that felicity and wretchedness depend on how deeds end.

It has been said that his words at the end of the hadith, “By Allah, besides whom there is no god, one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise…” to the end of the hadith, are an interpolation (mudraj) of Ibn Masʿūd’s own words;
that is how Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated it, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ibn Masʿūd, as his own saying. But this meaning has also been reported from the Prophet ﷺ by a number of routes.
In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from Sahl ibn Saʿd, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Actions are only by their endings.”
In the Ṣaḥīḥ of Ibn Ḥibbān, from ʿĀʾishah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Actions are only by their endings.”

Also in it, from Muʿāwiyah, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Actions are only by their endings, like a vessel: if the top of it is good, the bottom of it is good, and if the top of it is bad, the bottom of it is bad.”
In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “A man does the deeds of the people of Paradise for a long time,

and then his deeds are sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire; and a man does the deeds of the people of the Fire for a long time, and then his deeds are sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise.”

Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “You lose nothing by not being impressed with anyone until you see how his life is sealed, for the one who acts may spend a period of his life,

or a stretch of his time, doing a righteous deed such that, were he to die on it, he would enter Paradise; then he changes and does an evil deed. And the servant may spend a stretch of his time doing an evil deed such that, were he to die on it, he would enter the Fire; then he changes and does a righteous deed.”

He also recorded, from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “A man does the deeds of the people of Paradise while he is written in the Book as one of the people of the Fire; and shortly before his death he changes,

does the deeds of the people of the Fire, dies and enters the Fire. And a man does the deeds of the people of the Fire while he is written in the Book as one of the people of Paradise; and shortly before his death he changes, does the deeds of the people of Paradise, dies and enters it.”

Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī and al-Tirmidhī recorded, from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us with two books in his hand and said: “Do you know what these two books are?”

We said: No, O Messenger of Allah, unless you tell us. He said of the one in his right hand: “This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, in which are the names of the people of Paradise and the names of their fathers and tribes;

then it is totalled up at the last of them, so none will ever be added to them or taken from them.” Then he said of the one in his left hand: “This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, in which are the names of the people of the Fire and the names of their fathers and tribes;

then it is totalled up at the last of them, so none will ever be added to them or taken from them.” His Companions said: Then what is action for, O Messenger of Allah, if it is a matter already settled?

He said: “Keep to the right course and come as near to it as you can, for the person of Paradise will have his life sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, whatever he may have done; and the person of the Fire will have his life sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire,

whatever he may have done.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a gesture with his hands and cast them aside, and said: “Your Lord has finished with the servants: a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.”
This hadith has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ by a number of routes. Al-Ṭabarānī recorded it from the hadith of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ,

and added to it: “The person of Paradise has his life sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the person of the Fire has his life sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, whatever he may have done. The people of felicity may be led along the path of the people of wretchedness until it is said:

How like them they are — no, they are of them! Then felicity overtakes them and rescues them. And the people of wretchedness may be led along the path of the people of felicity until it is said: How like them they are — no, they are of them! Then wretchedness overtakes them.

Whomever Allah has written as happy in the Mother of the Book, He does not take out of this world until He has employed him in a deed that brings him felicity before his death, even if only for the interval between two milkings of a she-camel.” Then he said: “Actions are by their endings; actions are by their endings.”
Al-Bazzār also recorded it in his Musnad with this meaning, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Sahl ibn Saʿd: The Prophet ﷺ met the idolaters in battle, and among his Companions was a man who would not let any straggler or stray enemy go without pursuing him and striking him with his sword. They said: None of us has done as well today as So-and-so.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is of the people of the Fire.” A man among the people said: I will keep with him. He followed him, and the man was badly wounded and hastened his death: he set his sword on the ground with its point between his breasts,

then bore down on his sword and killed himself. The man went out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and told him the story. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“A man does the deeds of the people of Paradise, as far as appears to people, while he is of the people of the Fire; and a man does the deeds of the people of the Fire, as far as appears to people, while he is of the people of Paradise.” In one of his versions al-Bukhārī added: “Actions are only by their endings.”

His words “as far as appears to people” indicate that the inner reality of the matter may be otherwise, and that an evil ending comes about because of some hidden flaw in the servant that people do not see, whether from an evil deed or the like;

that hidden trait brings about an evil ending at death. Likewise a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire while within him there is some hidden trait of goodness, and that trait prevails over him at the end of his life and brings him a good ending.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Rawwād said: I was present at the death of a man who was being prompted to say “There is no god but Allah”, and the last thing he said was: He disbelieves in what you are saying — and he died on that. I asked about him, and it turned out that he was addicted to wine.
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to say: Beware of sins, for it was they that brought him down.

In sum, endings are the legacy of what was decreed beforehand, and all of that is already in the prior Writ. That is why the Salaf feared evil endings so intensely, and some of them were disquieted at the mention of what had been decreed beforehand.
It has been said: The hearts of the righteous are attached to endings; they say: With what will our lives be sealed?
And the hearts of those brought near are attached to what was decreed beforehand; they say: What has been decreed for us beforehand?

One of the Companions wept at his death, and was asked why. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah the Exalted took His creation in two handfuls and said: These are in Paradise, and these are in the Fire,” and I do not know in which of the two handfuls I was.
One of the Salaf said: Nothing has made eyes weep as the prior Writ has made them weep.
Sufyān said to one of the righteous: Has Allah’s knowledge of you ever made you weep?
The man said to him: You have left me never able to rejoice again.

Sufyān was intensely disquieted by what was decreed beforehand and by endings. He would weep and say: I fear that I am written wretched in the Mother of the Book; and he would weep and say: I fear being stripped of faith at death.
Mālik ibn Dīnār would stand the whole night holding his beard and saying: My Lord, You know who will dwell in Paradise and who in the Fire; in which of the two abodes is Mālik’s home?

Ḥātim al-Aṣamm said: Whoever’s heart is empty of remembering four perils is deluded and not safe from wretchedness. The first is the peril of the Day of the Covenant, when He said: These are in Paradise and I do not care,

and these are in the Fire and I do not care — and he does not know in which of the two parties he was. The second is when he was created in three darknesses and the angel was called upon to [write] felicity or wretchedness, and he does not know whether he is among the wretched or the happy.
The third is remembering the terror of what he will behold [at death]: he does not know whether he will be given glad tidings of Allah’s pleasure or of His wrath.
The fourth is the day when people come forth in scattered groups, and he does not know which of the two paths he will be made to take.
Sahl al-Tustarī said: The seeker fears being tried with sins; the one who knows Allah fears being tried with disbelief.

That is why the Companions and the righteous Salaf after them feared hypocrisy for themselves and were intensely disquieted and alarmed by it. The believer fears the lesser hypocrisy for himself, and fears that it may overcome him at the end and carry him into the greater hypocrisy,
since, as has been seen, hidden evil flaws bring about an evil ending. The Prophet ﷺ used often to say in his supplication:
“O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.” It was said to him: O Prophet of Allah, we have believed in you and in what you brought; do you fear for us?
He said: “Yes. Hearts are between two of the fingers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He turns them as He wills.” Imam Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī recorded it from the hadith of Anas.

Imam Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī recorded, from the hadith of Umm Salamah, that the Prophet ﷺ used often to say in his supplication: “O Allah, O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.” I said: O Messenger of Allah, do hearts really turn?

He said: “Yes. There is no human being of the children of Ādam created by Allah the Exalted but his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah: if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wills, He keeps it upright, and if He wills, He makes it swerve.

So we ask Allah our Lord not to make our hearts swerve after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us mercy from Himself; indeed, He is the Bestower.” She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not teach me a supplication to make for myself?

He said: “Yes, indeed. Say: O Allah, Lord of the Prophet Muḥammad, forgive me my sin, remove the anger of my heart, and protect me from the misleading trials for as long as You keep me alive.” There are many hadiths with this meaning.
Muslim recorded, from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

“The hearts of the children of Ādam, all of them, are between two of the fingers of the All-Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic, like a single heart, which He directs wherever He wills.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience.”
